title: Somewhere, Coding Stopped Being Allowed to Be Fun
why_read: A personal essay about the emotional toll of AI hype on programmers' enjoyment of coding, more reflective opinion than technical content.
analysis: This is a first-person reflective piece responding to another blog post about whether it's still okay to enjoy programming amid narratives that AI is making the craft obsolete. It doesn't contain technical content, code, or research findings, but rather explores the psychological and cultural pressure some developers feel from the 'AI will replace you' discourse. This kind of content can resonate emotionally with readers experiencing similar anxiety, but it offers little actionable or technical value for a professional digest. It's reasonably well written but belongs more in a general career or wellness newsletter than a technical one.
